transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you too, Dr. Smith. Well, what brought me in is... I find myself checking things over and over before I can move on with my day. It's usually the same things—boxes, my lists, the drawers around our condo. I just keep checking them. 

The frustrating part is that I know perfectly well I already looked. But I do it anyway, even when my wife is right there waiting for me to just leave it be so we can go. It's just become a bit of a nuisance, really, and I figured it was time to talk to someone about it.
When you feel the need to check these items, do you experience any specific thoughts or feelings of dread that prompt you to do it?

Well, I wouldn't really call it a feeling of dread. It's more of a... a nagging thought. I just keep thinking that maybe I threw away something important from my old teaching files, or that I put a needed tool in the wrong box. 

I try to tell myself it's highly unlikely. I know it is. But the thought just comes back anyway, and it makes it really hard to settle down and relax until I go look.
How much time out of your day would you say you spend checking these items?

I'm not entirely sure, to be honest. I've never really timed it. 

It's not like it takes up hours and hours of my day... it's really just a few minutes here and there. You know, maybe five or ten minutes before we head out the door, or a little bit of time when I'm putting things away in the study. It's more of a nuisance because it interrupts what I'm actually trying to do, rather than something that takes up my whole afternoon.

Aside from the checking behaviors you mentioned, do you also experience persistent, intrusive thoughts or ideas that you find distressing, even if they don't lead you to perform a specific action or check anything?

No, not really. It's just the thoughts about misplacing things or throwing out something I shouldn't have. I don't have other kinds of upsetting thoughts that get stuck in my head like that. It's pretty much just focused on the boxes and my files.

When you are performing these checks, do you feel that they are truly necessary to prevent a negative outcome, or do you feel like they are excessive and unreasonable despite your inability to stop doing them?

Well, I know they're excessive. I mean, I know perfectly well I already looked. It's just... I find myself checking the same boxes, my lists, the condo drawers over and over before I can move on. 

I know it's not truly necessary. My wife will be waiting for me to just leave it be, and I know I should. But I just can't seem to stop myself from doing it anyway.
When you are checking these items, do you feel a need to get them 'just right' or in a specific order, or is it strictly because you are worried about losing or misplacing something?

No, it's not about getting things lined up or in a certain order. I don't care about that at all. It's really just the fear that I've lost something important, like a document or a receipt. I'm just checking to make sure it's still there, not trying to make it look neat or anything.
How much does this checking routine cause you actual distress or prevent you from doing things you would otherwise want to be doing?

Well, it definitely gets in the way. Unpacking the condo, for instance... it's just taken much longer than it really should. And I've been putting off my preparation for the tutoring I do at the library, and even just my regular hobbies. I just feel like I can't move on to those things until everything is verified enough. So, yes, it's frustrating because it stops me from doing what I actually want to be doing with my day.
How long have you been experiencing these persistent, repetitive urges to check your belongings?

You know, I'm not entirely sure exactly when it started. It feels like it's been going on for a little while now, but I couldn't give you a specific date or anything. It just sort of... crept up on me, I suppose.
Looking back, would you say these checking habits have been happening for at least six months, or has this been a more recent development?

I really couldn't say for sure if it's been six months. I haven't been keeping track of the time, to be honest. It might be that long, or maybe a bit less... I just don't have a clear timeline in my head for when it really started becoming an issue.
When these checking behaviors occur, do you find that they cause you significant emotional distress, such as feeling anxious or upset beyond just being annoyed?

I wouldn't really call it significant emotional distress, no. I mean, I'm not... I don't get terribly anxious or deeply upset about it. It's really just what you said—it's annoying. I get a bit frustrated with myself that I have to keep going back over things, but I'm not panicking or anything like that. It's mostly just a nuisance.
Are there any other types of repetitive thoughts or behaviors that you experience, or is your experience strictly limited to this checking of files and belongings?

Well, it's mostly the checking, but... I do get these thoughts that just won't go away. I keep thinking, you know, that I might have thrown out something important from my old teaching files. Or that I put a tool I need in the wrong box out in the garage. I tell myself it's probably fine, but the thought just keeps coming back. It makes it hard to just sit down and relax until I go look.
When you finally give in and perform the check, do you feel a temporary sense of relief or a reduction in that nagging feeling before the thought eventually returns?

Yeah, I suppose I do get a bit of relief. It settles the thought for a minute so I can finally move on. But... well, that's exactly what brought me in. I find myself checking those same boxes, my lists, the drawers around the condo, just over and over again. 

I'll do it even though I know perfectly well I already looked. My wife will be standing right there, waiting for me to just leave it be and go, but I still have to go back and do the check just to get that nagging feeling to stop.
